criteria.text: Treatment of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), the closed indication in this Alaska Medicaid criteria PDF.
Patient is an adult, 18 years or older (FDA labeled age; approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist or oncologist (approval criterion 2).
PNH diagnosis confirmed by flow cytometry diagnostic testing (approval criterion 3).
Patient has at least one qualifying indication for PNH therapy (approval criterion 4).
Documented baseline serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) AND hemoglobin <10.5 g/dL (approval criterion 5).
Appropriate vaccinations against encapsulated bacteria (e.g. meningococcal) at least 14 days prior to the first dose (approval criterion 6).
Not combined with another PNH complement inhibitor (e.g. Soliris or Ultomiris), unless in a 4-week Soliris to Empaveli cross-titration period (denial criterion 2).
No unresolved serious infection caused by encapsulated bacteria (denial criterion 3).
Prescriber is enrolled in the REMS program (denial criterion 4).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Empaveli (pegcetacoplan) Criteria Version 1: Original 10/10/2022; Approval 11/18/2022; Effective 1/2/2023. The effective_date remains 2023-01-02.

Encoded: the closed PNH indication, adult age, approval criteria 1-6, and denial criteria 2-4 as approval-blocking predicates. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. Baseline LDH and hemoglobin <10.5 g/dL are a combined attestation, without numeric lab predicates.

Duration (notes only): initial approval 6 months; reauthorization 12 months with chart notes showing improvement or stabilization on the requested medication, such as decreased RBC transfusion requirement, stabilization/improvement of hemoglobin, reduction of LDH, or stabilization/improvement of symptoms.
Quantity limit: 10 vials per 30 days (1080 mg administered every 3 days); HCPCS J3490. Quantity metadata is recorded, but quantity and dosing are not evaluated as predicates.

Cautions: Empaveli may predispose individuals to serious, life-threatening, or fatal infections caused by encapsulated bacteria. Prescriber REMS enrollment and absence of unresolved serious encapsulated-bacteria infection are required attestations.
Caution (notes only): silica reagents in coagulation panels may cause artificially prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT).
Approval durations, reauthorization response documentation, quantity, dosing, and cautions require manual review; this pack remains partial.
No PDL hit; pdl_status remains unknown. Soliris/Ultomiris is a linked complement inhibitor alternative for PNH overlap only; its own criteria require separate review.
